title: Criminology, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. Real gap fixed in the shared crim_catalog.json (benefits any future major reusing it): CRIM 249 and CRIM 250W had empty prereq_groups despite the bulletin's own 'Critical Sequencing Note' stating CRIM 12/SOC 12 -> CRIM 249 -> CRIM 250W MUST be followed -- added CRIM 249's real prereq (CRIM 12 or SOC 12) and concurrent (CRIM 100 or CRIM 100H), and CRIM 250W's real prereq (CRIM 249 and STAT 200), sourced directly from the department's own course-description pages. 'LA 283', named in the bulletin's own Second Year Spring semester, could not be confirmed to exist (same finding as the History B.A. build) -- replaced with a generic 'Second-Year Liberal Arts Seminar' slot. UPDATE after the prereq-parser fix: the freshly re-scraped catalogs/crim_catalog.json now shows CRIM 249 and CRIM 250W with EMPTY prereq_groups again (the CRIM 12/SOC 12 -> CRIM 249 -> CRIM 250W -> STAT 200 chain described above is no longer present in the on-disk catalog data as of this pass -- flagged for human review, not re-added here since catalogs/*.json is out of scope for this fix). The real gap actually hit by this pass was STAT 200 itself: its real prereq_groups require MATH 21 (which itself needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3), none of which were anywhere in this plan -- added the MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 chain explicitly (Semesters 1-3) so STAT 200 (Semester 2 on the flowchart) becomes schedulable; the simulator naturally defers STAT 200 to the real term it becomes eligible. HANDBOOK VERIFICATION PASS: found the Department of Sociology and Criminology's own real degree checksheets (sociology.la.psu.edu/wp-content/uploads/.../CRIM_B.A.-Checksheet.pdf and .../Race-Ethnicity-Gender-Course-List-.pdf, both 'Last updated in December 2024'/'October 2024' -- more current and granular than the bulletin page these plans were built from). Real gaps fixed: (1) 'Race/Ethnicity/Gender Course' (2 occurrences) was a fully generic, unenumerated slot -- the department publishes a real 70-course list (AFAM/AMST/ANTH/CAS/CI/CMLIT/CRIM/ENGL/HIST/JST/LHR/LTNST/PHIL/PLSC/PSYCH/SOC/WMNST courses); wired both occurrences with the real list via a match pattern so a student who reports one of these courses is actually credited, instead of it silently falling into 'extra courses'. (2) '4XX CRIM Core Course' (2 occurrences) was never distinguished from any other 400-level CRIM course -- the checksheet names an exact 8-course Core list (CRIM/CRIMJ/SOC 413, CRIM 430, CRIM/CRIMJ 432, CRIM 435, CRIM/CRIMJ 451, CRIM/CRIMJ/WMNST 453, CRIM/CRIMJ/SOC 467, CRIM/PPOL 490); wired via match pattern. (3) '4XX CRIM Course' (non-core, 2 occurrences) confirmed by the checksheet as genuinely open ('Any 400-level Criminology course can be used as a Non-Core 400-Level CRIM Course') -- wired with a real CRIM 4xx match pattern so it's schedulable/creditable instead of a bare placeholder. Remaining generic Gen Ed/B.A. Fields/World Cultures/Elective pools stay generic -- the checksheet itself leaves those open ('see advising').
